extraction_method: AST selected all @mcp.tool() wrapper definitions from server.py unchanged and executed their registrations in an isolated FastMCP instance; called local list_tools() with repository-locked mcp 1.28.1 and Pydantic 2.13.4. No wrapper body, repository startup/config import, credential read, client creation, or remote tool call executed. Inspected complete source tree for registrations and implementations.
limitations: Runtime BigQuery execution and dataset availability were not tested. Local introspection bypasses lifespan/imports intentionally; registration definitions and annotations are executed unchanged.
Project permits broad dependency versions; schemas are verified against its uv.lock versions, not every permitted version.
reason: All three unconditionally registered Google Trends tools have complete locally verified input schemas and implemented BigQuery queries.

tools.name: buscar_termos_em_alta_tool
tools.behavior: Queries bigquery-public-data.google_trends.international_top_terms for a country with week >= data_limite, ordered by newest week then ascending rank. Returns term, nullable score, and rank for each row; no result limit or deduplication.
validation_notes: Implementation uppercases pais, then restricts it to AU, BR, CA, DE, ES, FR, GB, IN, JP, US; this restriction is not an input-schema enum.
All input fields are required strings with no defaults, nullable variants, bounds, patterns, or date formats in the schema. additionalProperties is unspecified.
Dates are not parsed or validated locally. They are passed as STRING BigQuery query parameters, and any query/type/date failure becomes BigQueryError.
An initialized BigQuery client is required for execution; startup validates GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT and creates an ADC-authenticated client. No client or server context is caller-supplied.
No rows yields an empty list.

tools.name: comparar_termo_tool
tools.behavior: Queries bigquery-public-data.google_trends.international_top_terms for one case-insensitively matched term and country, with week BETWEEN data_inicio AND data_fim, ordered by ascending week. Returns week, term, nullable score, and rank. Despite its name it does not compare multiple terms.
validation_notes: Implementation uppercases pais, then restricts it to AU, BR, CA, DE, ES, FR, GB, IN, JP, US; this restriction is not an input-schema enum.
All input fields are required strings with no defaults, nullable variants, bounds, patterns, or date formats in the schema. additionalProperties is unspecified.
Dates are not parsed or validated locally. They are passed as STRING BigQuery query parameters, and any query/type/date failure becomes BigQueryError.
An initialized BigQuery client is required for execution; startup validates GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT and creates an ADC-authenticated client. No client or server context is caller-supplied.
No rows yields an empty list.
termo is lowercased before exact SQL equality; there is no empty-term or date-order validation. SQL BETWEEN includes both endpoints.
